ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has two side-by-side schematic diagrams of abrupt p-n junction diodes. The left side is Diode 1, labeled with capacitance C1, and 10^14 cm^-3 is written in both the p region and the n region; the right side is Diode 2, labeled with capacitance C2, and 10^16 cm^-3 is written in both the p region and the n region. Therefore both diodes are symmetrically doped on the p and n sides, respectively NA1 = ND1 = 10^14 cm^-3 and NA2 = ND2 = 10^16 cm^-3. Reasoning: The depletion layer width of an abrupt p-n junction under reverse bias is W = sqrt((2 eps/q)(1/NA + 1/ND)(VR + Vbi)). The given reverse bias voltage is much greater than the built-in potential, so under the same reverse bias one can approximately compare only the doping term. For symmetric doping, NA = ND = N, therefore (1/NA + 1/ND) = 2/N, so W is proportional to 1/sqrt(N). The junction capacitance C = eps A / W, and under the same structure and the same area C is proportional to sqrt(N). Therefore C2/C1 = sqrt(N2/N1) = sqrt(10^16 / 10^14) = sqrt(100) = 10.
